title: When, Blest Redeemer, Thou Art Near
description: When, Blest Redeemer, Thou Art Near in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 154, “The Presence of Jesus”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: When, blest Re-deem-er, thou art near, The soul en-joys a sa-cred peace: Thy pre-sence calms our ev-ery fear, And gives from ev-ery doubt re-lease.

lines: When, blest Redeemer, thou art near,
The soul enjoys a sacred peace:
Thy presence calms our every fear,
And gives from every doubt release.
Be with us now, in truth and love,
In strength that conquers every sin;
O, cleanse, and bless, and lift above,
And may thy cross our hearts still win.
In suffering may we strength receive
From memory of thy victory won;
In doubt our drooping hopes revive; —
Thus be thy presence with us shown!
Be ever near our spirits, Lord;
And, drawn by sympathy, may we
Still, through thy cross, thy life, thy word,
In faith and love come near to thee!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
